answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation: every agent identity must lock a deposit with a delayed withdrawal, so an attacker spinning up an umber of shadow clones dilutes their own capital across each fake. Peers audit behavior at a rotating review summit, flagging identities whose activity patterns correlate too tightly to be independent, and slash the deposits of confirmed sybils. Honest agents risk almost nothing beyond a bond, while each clone costs the attacker real money — anchoring trust in economic skin in the game rather than in cheap account creation.
